data.label: Support staff
data.description: Support agents using a browser. A client reference, not provisioned.

data.label: Staff sign-in
data.description: Authenticates staff before the console and passes a verified identity downstream. The identity provider is still to be decided.

data.label: Staff console
data.description: Web UI. Shows the ticket, the draft answer with citations, and Send/Edit/Escalate actions. A human sends every reply.

data.label: Assistant orchestrator
data.description: Gets ticket context, runs retrieval scoped to the staff member's permissions, calls the read-only CRM adapter and drafts a grounded answer. It abstains when no source supports an answer. A policy check blocks refunds and record changes and routes them to escalation.

data.label: Synthetic ticket queue
data.description: Existing synthetic ticketing system that supplies open tickets.

data.label: Approved knowledge
data.description: Private bucket holding approved articles and their ACL metadata.

data.label: Authorised retrieval
data.description: Indexes the approved knowledge and filters results by user/group ACL. Returns passages with their source IDs for citation.

data.label: CRM read-only adapter
data.description: Uses a read-only service account to fetch only the customer fields this ticket needs. It has no write or refund operations.

data.label: Existing CRM
data.description: The customer system of record. Stays outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Answer model
data.description: Drafts answers using only the passages it is given. Mocked in the local test. The model version, region and quota are not verified.

data.label: Human escalation
data.description: Routes refunds, record-change requests and low-confidence cases to a supervisor queue/ticket note. A person decides.

data.label: Audit & monitoring
data.description: Records who asked, which sources were used, the draft and blocked actions, plus latency and error alerts.

brief.application: Use Google Cloud for this synthetic architecture qualification. Assist support staff using a synthetic ticket queue, approved knowledge and customer records from an existing CRM. Include authorized retrieval, grounded answer drafting, a staff interface and human escalation. Never issue refunds or modify customer records automatically. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

lastAsked.beginner: For example “SharePoint and a shared drive, about 20,000 files”.

requirements.statement: The assistant must not issue refunds or create, update or delete CRM records. Such requests must be routed to human escalation.
requirements.rationale: An automated financial or record change could harm customers. Enforcing read-only access plus a policy check limits the blast radius.
requirements.basis: User: "Never issue refunds or modify customer records automatically."

requirements.statement: Retrieval must return only knowledge the signed-in staff member is permitted to see, and must fail closed when the identity is unknown.
requirements.rationale: Without permission filtering, drafts could leak restricted content.

requirements.statement: Every draft must cite its approved knowledge or CRM sources, abstain when unsupported, and be sent only after a person reviews it.
requirements.rationale: Grounding and human review reduce wrong answers reaching customers. Mocked tests cannot prove this, so a real model evaluation is needed.
requirements.basis: User: "grounded answer drafting, a staff interface and human escalation"

decisions.subject: design.google-cloud-support-assistant-end-to-end-draft
decisions.title: Google Cloud support assistant – end-to-end draft
decisions.context: Scope: staff assistant over a synthetic ticket queue, approved knowledge and existing CRM (read-only). It includes authorised retrieval, grounded drafting, a staff interface, human escalation and audit. Assumptions: the region is not selected; model access, quotas and region availability are not verified; GCP components are design-only (no native generator yet); the CRM and ticket queue are existing systems. Refunds and record changes are excluded by design: there is no write path to the CRM.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.
